strengths: MU-Mis introduces an interesting input-sensitivity objective that requires only the pretrained model and forgetting data, avoiding retained-data replay and stored training trajectories.

Experiments cover full-class, subclass, and random-subset deletion, with retraining and several relevant baselines. Class-deletion results show promising utility preservation: on CIFAR-100, retained accuracy remains 76.32% versus 76.36% before unlearning, while forgetting-class accuracy reaches zero.

The claimed symmetry of g_k g'_k^T does not generally hold for multiclass outputs, undermining the identification of contribution with sensitivity. Furthermore, individually small cross-sample terms do not imply their sum is negligible, and input perturbation is not equivalent to sample deletion.

Equation (1) admits improvements unrelated to forgetting. Adding the same input-dependent offset to every logit preserves all softmax probabilities but changes the proposed loss. For example, logits (x, 0) shifted to ((1-M)x, -Mx) preserve predictions while the target-minus-other squared-gradient objective becomes 1-2M, which is unbounded below. Critical implementation details are missing. The task-dependent stopping threshold delta and its selection procedure are unspecified. Algorithm 1 initializes the running loss to zero but never accumulates it, and its nested repeat/iteration structure leaves termination unclear. The analysis also uses sums of unsquared sensitivities over irrelevant classes, whereas implementation samples one class and uses squared norms, changing the relative weighting without validation.
